title: Vendor onboarding: approval pathways & technical onboarding sync
summary: Kickoff between Redwood and Pinecrest to align on vendor onboarding approvals, MSA/DPA redlines, SSO/KMS requirements, and pricing approval timeline. Discussed hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs and next steps for legal review and pilot procurement.
topics: Pricing approval path and PO timeline
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~56m
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Aisha (Redwood); Daniel, Priya, Tom, Sara (Pinecrest)
Links shared: onboarding-checklist v2 (drive link), security-pack.zip (link), draft pricing spreadsheet (link)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Daniel Ruiz: Hey all, Daniel here, procurement.
[00:11] Priya Nair: Priya, security and compliance.
[00:13] Tom Keller: Tom, infra.
[00:15] Sara Bloom: Sara, legal counsel.
[00:18] Liam O'Rourke: Liam from Redwood SE. I'll do the technical bits.
[00:21] Aisha Patel: Aisha, solutions eng, happy to jump in on onboarding flow.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today is to align on approval pathway — what doc owners we need, priority redlines in the MSA/DPA, plus technical blockers for onboarding and what the pilot acceptance criteria look like.

[02:05] Daniel Ruiz: To be blunt, our procurement committee needs to know two things: 1) are there any exceptions to our standard MSA we need to route, and 2) cost bucket — is this CapEx or OpEx and what's the expected monthly run rate for a pilot.

[03:12] Maya Chen: Understood. On the MSA side we've seen typical redlines around audit rights, indemnity caps, and data residency. We can highlight those in a redline doc; we'll flag which are deal-breakers vs. negotiable. On pricing, we have the hosted model pricing sheet I can share — and also a dedicated/private deployment price estimate if you need VPC/on-prem.

[04:45] Priya Nair: For us, data residency matters — patient data. We need options for EU residency and the ability to run inference in our VPC for PHI. Also SOC 2 plus independent pen test report and certs.

[05:30] Liam O'Rourke: Right; operationally, Redwood Private supports a VPC-hosted control plane and on-prem packaging. There's also our Dedicated capacity which sits in a customer-dedicated GPU pool. Small note — sorry if transcript flips names — some customers call it "Redwood Dedicate" in notes.

[06:15] Tom Keller: If we go private, what's the KMS story? We require customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS for key rotation.

[06:25] Aisha Patel: We have KMS integrations documented. We can do KMS via our supported KMS providers and we can also bring-your-own-HSM for Private installs. We'll send the KMS integration diagram.

[08:02] Sara Bloom: On the DPA, we have two specific asks: first, stricter subprocessor notice and second, breach notification timelines — we're standard at 72 hours.

[08:30] Maya Chen: We usually support 72-hour notification, plus a subprocessor list that we update quarterly. We can add a clause for 30-day notice for material subprocessor changes — we'll flag that in the redline.

[10:01] Priya Nair: Also logging and audit: we need exportable audit logs retaining 1 year for our internal compliance. How feasible is that?

[10:22] Liam O'Rourke: We surface audit logs via the Console with configurable retention in Dedicated/Private. Hosted tier has a default retention but we can offer longer retention as an add-on. There might be a cost delta.

[12:05] Daniel Ruiz: Pricing approvals — our finance gate wants an itemized run rate and a 3-month pilot cap. Can you provide estimated token throughput and unit cost so we can map to our budget?

[13:00] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll produce a pilot SOW + cost worksheet. Liam, can you outline typical token perf for a standard chat workload?

[13:15] Liam O'Rourke: For the open models we often see median latencies in the 150–350ms range per token with modest batching; throughput will depend on sequence length. For Dedicated, throughput is more predictable because you get reserved GPUs; private can be tuned to match. Note: numbers vary by model and quantization — we'll attach the benchmark sheet (link).

[15:40] Tom Keller: Are there SLAs for latency and uptime? Our ops team requires 99.9% for production.

[16:05] Aisha Patel: Our Dedicated tier has SLA-backed uptime and a latency SLO playbook. For hosted we offer best-effort with published performance profiles; for 99.9% you'd typically need Dedicated or Private. There are options for credits if SLA is missed — we'll include SLA language and credit matrix in the draft.

[18:20] Sara Bloom: On indemnity, we need to check dollar caps and carve outs for gross negligence — that's standard in our MSA. Any flexibility?

[19:00] Maya Chen: We can discuss caps; there are enterprise terms we can propose. We'll mark which sections are commonly negotiated.

[20:12] Priya Nair: Regarding SSO, we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. We also expect RBAC and least privilege.

[20:28] Liam O'Rourke: SAML and SCIM supported. RBAC is available in Console, with token-level permissions and route-based controls. We'll include the RBAC matrix.

[22:45] Daniel Ruiz: What's the typical procurement timeline once legal gets the redlines? Ours usually takes 3–6 weeks if there are no major exceptions.

[23:10] Maya Chen: That matches what we've seen. To expedite, we often run a parallel legal and security review — send security pack while legal reviews MSA redlines.

[24:55] Priya Nair: We'll need the security questionnaire backfilled (SIG/CAIQ). Can you commit to a date to return that?

[25:10] Aisha Patel: We can return a completed CAIQ within 5 business days. We'll attach our SOC 2 report (redacted).

[26:40] Tom Keller: For the pilot, acceptance criteria — we want throughput at X qps for inference, latency p95 under 800ms, and no data exfil alerts. Can the pilot be in our EU region?

[27:05] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, we can spin pilot in an EU region with either Hosted EU tenancy or a Private VPC in eu-central. Need to confirm your exact region preference.

[28:30] Maya Chen: On procurement-side approvals, who's the final signatory? Daniel?

[28:40] Daniel Ruiz: Procurement signs, but the legal counsel (Sara) needs the final MSA sign-off and finance signs the PO.

[29:12] Sara Bloom: We'll be looking at liability and data protection sections closely. Also want a clear SOW for the pilot with acceptance test cases.

[31:00] Maya Chen: We'll produce a draft pilot SOW with test cases and an itemized pricing sheet. We'll also send a redline MSA/DPA with comments keyed to the clause owners.

[32:20] Priya Nair: One more question on retention: will Redwood ever index or store PHI in ways that might be used to train models? We need a contractual assurance that customer content is not used for training unless opt-in.

[32:45] Aisha Patel: We have a customer-data-use clause that prohibits using customer data for training without opt-in; we'll include explicit contractual language. Might be transcribed as "not used for train" in the notes — apologies.

[34:15] Tom Keller: Networking — do you support VPC peering or private endpoints?

[34:30] Liam O'Rourke: Both. Private supports VPC peering and private endpoints. We'll send a network topology diagram.

[36:05] Daniel Ruiz: On billing approvals, do you accept NET30 PO? Our finance prefers standard net terms.

[36:20] Maya Chen: We can accept NET30 with the enterprise contract. We'll note billing contact and invoicing flow in the SOW.

[38:12] Sara Bloom: We'll circulate a redline with comments once we get the initial MSA. Timeline: legal first pass within two weeks, procurement gets PO within following week.

[39:50] Maya Chen: Helpful. For the pilot timeline, what's target start date?

[40:05] Daniel Ruiz: Ideally by mid-February, assuming approvals in January.

[40:20] Aisha Patel: That's feasible. Our ramp plan: week 0 deploy env, week 1 smoke tests, week 2 run load scenarios and acceptance tests. We can support with two SE days for onboarding during pilot.

[42:55] Priya Nair: Please note we require a penetration test report for the environment if it's Dedicated/Private. Is that provided by Redwood or do we need to perform our own?

[43:12] Liam O'Rourke: We provide recent pen test reports for our managed components; for Private installs on-prem, customers often run their own certs and pentests. We'll clarify in the security pack.

[45:00] Tom Keller: One practical ask: include clear rollback/failure modes in the SOW — if latency exceeds X we want auto-fallback to a lower-cost model or a safe-mode.

[45:20] Maya Chen: We can document fallback policies; Redwood has automatic fallback to a compatible model variant — we'll capture config options.

[46:55] Daniel Ruiz: Any competitors to be aware of in our evaluation? We're also looking at other incumbents.

[47:05] Maya Chen: I'll be transparent: Anthropic and some managed customers build on OpenAI or self-hosted infra. We'll provide a competitive summary sheet — pros/cons.

[48:40] Sara Bloom: For the DPA, also provide subprocessor list and EU data transfer mechanism — SCCs or adequacy.

[49:00] Aisha Patel: We'll include SCCs and confirm the transfer mechanism for Hosted EU. For Private in-EU, transfers shouldn't be necessary.

[50:25] Maya Chen: To summarize next steps—we'll: 1) send MSA/DPA redline draft, 2) deliver security pack including SOC2 and CAIQ in 5 business days, 3) share pilot SOW + pricing worksheet, 4) schedule a legal-only deep dive next week if needed.

[51:10] Daniel Ruiz: Sounds good. Add that we'll need the pricing sheet to present to the finance committee by Jan 28.

[52:40] Sara Bloom: We'll aim to do a first-pass legal review in two weeks. If there are any disputed terms we'll loop counsel.

[53:15] Priya Nair: Please redact any customer-identifying data in SOC2 before sending.

[53:30] Aisha Patel: Noted, we'll redact and send.

[54:05] Maya Chen: Any final questions?
[54:12] Tom Keller: No, thanks.
[54:20] Daniel Ruiz: Thanks all.
[54:25] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up via email and add the redlines to the drive link. Thanks everyone.
[56:00] Meeting end
next_steps: Redwood to send MSA/DPA redline (Maya) - target 2027-01-21
Redwood to deliver security pack (SOC2, CAIQ) - target 5 business days
Redwood to share pilot SOW + pricing worksheet (Liam/Aisha) - target 2027-01-22
Schedule legal-only deep dive with Sara - proposed 2027-01-25

Aisha Patel - Return completed CAIQ and redacted SOC2 - 2027-01-26
Liam O'Rourke - Attach benchmark and network diagram to pilot SOW - 2027-01-22
Daniel Ruiz - Confirm finance PO cadence and signatory - 2027-01-25
